name: Jehosheba
source_summary: Daughter of King Jehoram of Judah and wife of the priest Jehoiada, who rescued the infant prince Joash from her grandmother Athaliah's massacre of the royal family and hid him in the temple for six years, preserving the Davidic line.
family_friendly_summary: Jehosheba was a princess of Judah, the daughter of King Jehoram and sister of King Ahaziah. When Ahaziah died, his mother Athaliah seized the throne and tried to kill every member of the royal family so no one could challenge her. But Jehosheba secretly took her baby nephew Joash, along with his nurse, and hid him in a bedroom before Athaliah's soldiers could find him. She kept Joash hidden safely in the Temple for six years while Athaliah ruled. Because of Jehosheba's brave rescue, the line of King David was not wiped out, and Joash later became Judah's rightful king.
adult_story: Jehosheba was the daughter of King Jehoram of Judah, and, uniquely for a princess, the wife of the priest Jehoiada (2 Chronicles 22:11). When her brother King Ahaziah was killed by Jehu, their mother Athaliah seized the opportunity to eliminate every rival to the throne and "proceeded to destroy all the royal offspring" of the house of Judah (2 Kings 11:1). In the middle of this massacre, Jehosheba took Ahaziah's infant son Joash, stole him away from among the king's sons who were about to be put to death, and hid him along with his nurse in a bedroom (11:2). She kept him concealed in the house of the LORD for six years while Athaliah reigned over the land, unaware that an heir had survived (11:3; 2 Chronicles 22:11-12). Her husband Jehoiada later orchestrated Joash's public coronation as the rightful king at age seven, ending Athaliah's usurpation (2 Kings 11:4-16). Jehosheba's quiet, dangerous act of hiding one baby in a moment of royal bloodshed preserved the entire Davidic royal line at the point of its greatest threat -- without her, the promised line through which the Messiah would come could have been extinguished entirely in a single afternoon.
